payload.feature:
The slice on this branch is committed (758ec8b) and needs bringing to landing quality. What it holds: the README's quickstart became the 60-second bootstrap with a mermaid spine carrying the two measured budgets; ARCHITECTURE.md was rewritten around eight mermaid diagrams and under 1,900 words; decision 0037 (one source, two modalities) is proposed in docs/decisions with crates/brokkr-cli/tests/diagrams.rs as its enforcement binding; and dsh is named beside claude and codex wherever the agent CLIs are listed.

Scope: docs plus that one test file. No Rust outside crates/brokkr-cli/tests/diagrams.rs, no schema, adapter or recipe change, and implement nothing the decision proposes beyond the test that already exists. Keep the decision at Status: proposed. Do not name Looper or LaneTally anywhere on the changed pages. Every mermaid block must stay parseable by the diagrams test, the phase diagram must equal recipes/fast/policy.json's rules exactly, and the crate diagram must draw every crate with only declared dependencies as edges. The README stays under the front-page test's 150-line budget with its section order and proof strings intact.

result.notes: Framed intake task: validate and finalize the documentation slice (README/ARCHITECTURE/0037 decision) to landing quality. Task file at .forge/tasks/slice-pictures-landing-quality.md. The implementer runs the diagrams test suite to verify all four checks pass: architecture page budget/pictures count, phase diagram sync with policy.json, crate diagram sync with Cargo.toml, and no rendered images embedded outside assets/. No Rust changes except the test file itself, which is production code and must pass.

Verified the committed slice (758ec8b) already meets landing quality: all four crates/brokkr-cli/tests/diagrams.rs tests pass (phase diagram matches recipes/fast/policy.json exactly, crate diagram matches Cargo.toml deps, architecture page under budget with 8 mermaid blocks, no rendered images outside assets/). cargo test --workspace is fully green (0 failures). README.md is 101 lines (<150 budget), ARCHITECTURE.md is 1855 words with 8 mermaid diagrams (>=6 required, <1900/2000 word budget), decision 0037 stays Status: proposed, no Looper/LaneTally mentions on changed pages, and dsh is named beside claude and codex in both README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md. No code or doc changes were needed; working tree is clean at the existing commit, so nothing new was committed.

Ran `cargo test --workspace` at commit 758ec8b on a clean tree: every crate's suite passed (0 failed across all reported `test result: ok` blocks), including tests/diagrams.rs (4 passed — the mermaid enforcement binding for decision 0037), tests/machine_proof.rs (56 passed), and tests/differential.rs (corpus_parity_with_python_oracle ok, 3 passed total). Doc-tests all passed or had none to run. Then ran `cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self`: it finished cleanly, printing a full manifest with digest 960b99d6f5c84a6943704132c94853034f0cc467947846549d41e0b66b411aae and no error/violation/lint keys in the output. Both required steps green; no drift observed.

Reviewed everything since 758ec8b (docs + crates/brokkr-cli/tests/diagrams.rs) on all three dimensions. SECURITY: none. The slice touches no schema, adapter, recipe or engine code; the new test only reads files (no exec, no network, no journal write) and cannot be reached by seat results or driver output. I re-checked that the rewrite's condensed fail-closed prose is still true against the code: assert_phase_unavoidable in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs backs 'compile rejects any table where the protected review phase can be skipped on a path to a non-stop terminal'; trust_tier/binding_grant 'read closed on absence' and driver.confine survived the cut accurately; unknown driver messages fail closed per brokkr-protocol/src/lib.rs. The README's install path keeps its checksum-first form. Scope held: no Rust outside the test file, 0037 stays Status: proposed, nothing the decision proposes was implemented. CORRECTNESS, verified by hand rather than by the tests: the phase diagram's 14 unique edges and 7 states equal recipes/fast/policy.json's 22 rules exactly, and I also checked every transition LABEL (which the test ignores) against each rule's `when` clause — all accurate. The 97-case corpus claim equals wc -l fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson. scripts/bootstrap-bench.sh exists and is wired at .github/workflows/ci.yml:187, so the front page's two measured budgets are a real claim. brokkr-view's manifest is exactly brokkr-core + serde + serde_json as stated. FIXES APPLIED (committed 88e7db1, signed, tree clean; diagrams 4/4 and rename_guard 5/5 green after): 1. The crate diagram omitted brokkr-bridge -> brokkr-runtime, a declared dependency that NO drawn path implied (bridge reached only store), while the prose beside it asserts 'the edges a path already implies are left out'. The stated invariant was false and the picture understated the bridge's coupling to the engine loop. The test checks drawn-subset-of-declared, never the transitive-closure claim, so it could not catch this. Edge drawn; ARCHITECTURE.md now 1857 words, 8 blocks, both budgets intact. 2. Decision 0037 said 'nine diagrams' in Context and again in Consequences; ARCHITECTURE.md has eight (the slice's own commit message says eight). Corrected in both places - the decision that condemns drift was miscounting its own flagship page, and ruling 2's 'at least six' binding cannot catch it. RESIDUAL FINDINGS, not fixed (all low or info, none security): - [low] crates/brokkr-cli/tests/diagrams.rs:65 flowchart_edges mis-parses a chained arrow line. It takes the LAST arrow (rfind) for the right side and the FIRST opener for the left, so 'a --> b --> c' yields the single phantom edge a->c and silently drops a->b and b->c. The chain form is already used in this file (ARCHITECTURE.md:60, the journal diagram), so it is only luck that the crate block avoids it; the day someone writes 'cli --> runtime --> core' the enforcement binding for ruling 3 would assert a phantom edge and stop checking two real ones. Not fixed because rewriting the parser is beyond a small safe fix and would change edge extraction for other blocks - it wants its own diff with its own test. - [low] ARCHITECTURE.md:267 'The operating surface' presents itself as the binary's command list but omits 9 of the 28 visible subcommands declared in crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs: rerun, compare, recipes, agents, secrets, conclude, bridge, realms, keep-refs. Several (secrets, conclude, realms, rerun) are squarely operator-facing. This is an unchecked enumeration of a machine-owned structure on the very page decision 0037 makes its flagship - exactly ruling 3's concern, and it is not listed among the decision's Consequences debt. Pre-existing from main, but the slice edited that block (it added watch and muninn), so it is in scope to name. Not fixed: whether the list is curated-by-design or complete-by-contract is the operator's ruling, and either answer wants a test. - [info] The scope line 'do not name Looper or LaneTally anywhere on the changed pages' is met in spirit but not literally: four changed pages still carry pre-existing mentions the slice did not touch - docs/guides/README.md:15 (LaneTally), docs/decisions/README.md:54 (LaneTally's), docs/guides/quickstart.md:229 and :601 (Looper). The slice correctly REMOVED the one it owned (ARCHITECTURE.md's 'the LaneTally layer joins on' became 'a cost ledger can join on'). Left alone because these are substantive content about real integrations and deleting them is not this slice's job. - [info] crates/brokkr-cli/tests/diagrams.rs:266 living_surfaces_embed_no_rendered_pictures catches the Markdown image form and , but not reference-style images (![alt][ref] with a [ref]: ./x.png definition), /, or
